identity.description: Gladly is a customer service and support platform (conversations, inboxes, customer profiles, agents) with a REST API, webhooks, and chat SDKs. Matches the 'Support and Helpdesk' category and the gladly.com hint.
identity.identity_notes: Confirmed from Gladly's own docs domains (developer.gladly.com and help.gladly.com), which describe Gladly's agents, conversations, customers and inboxes. The gladly.com homepage itself was not fetched. Not to be confused with Ordergroove, which is a Gladly integration partner and appears in the migration pages.

auth.token_refresh: No refresh flow found. Tokens are static and rotated manually (the developer docs include a rotation procedure, per search summary, not verified).
auth.scopes_notes: No OAuth scopes. Access is governed by the user's API User permission, and an API token can be used to perform any API request without restriction (per developer docs).

access.production_restrictions: No self-serve developer signup found. Tokens are created by a Gladly user who has the API User permission, which appears to be enabled by a Gladly administrator. A sandbox is available, but if you do not already have one you must contact your Gladly CSM or Gladly Support to purchase it. Tokens are environment-specific.

read_ops: Conversation timelines, items, notes and topics
write_ops: Customer profile create, update and delete
Tasks with due dates and assignees
Freeform topic data attached to conversations
api.rate_limits: Default: 10 requests/second per method (GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE). Reports API: 10 requests/minute and 2 concurrent requests per organization. Response headers Ratelimit-Limit-Second and Ratelimit-Remaining-Second.
api.limitations: Only Basic auth with API token is documented. A token belongs to one user in one environment. Lookup API is a web service Gladly calls into your system, not a client call. The SDKs found are client-side chat SDKs (Web, iOS, Android) and Help Center customization, not a server-side API SDK. WebSocket was not confirmed in sources, so it is listed here only from the REST and webhook docs and should be removed if unsupported.

Pricing or contractual gating for API access and the sandbox is not stated in sources.
Rate-limit and webhook event details were taken from fetch summaries and should be checked on the live developer.gladly.com pages.
WebSocket support is not confirmed by any source fetched, so it may be wrong and should be removed unless verified.
